transcript.text: Every time I put the oven on it runs for a few minutes and then the trip switch goes and half the house loses power. Reset it 3 times tonight. Hotpoint built-in, about 9 years old. What could cause this?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
Please don't keep resetting the trip. Leave the appliance unplugged and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer before using it again. The most likely cause is a heating element whose insulation is breaking down and leaking current to earth once it gets hot. That is a very common pattern: it heats normally for a few minutes, then trips the RCD/circuit and takes out part of the house. Less commonly, it is damaged wiring or a burnt connection around an element; the control board is possible but lower down the list. The function that was selected does not prove that particular element is at fault, because oven electrical circuits can share connections. Do not use or reset it again. It needs a qualified appliance engineer or electrician to carry out an insulation/leakage test and inspect the elements and their wiring; that is the only reliable way to identify the failed component safely. If there has been any burning smell, smoke, or heat damage around the oven, isolate it at the cooker switch as well and tell the engineer.

candidates: Heating element insulation leaking to earth as it warms up (high)
Damaged element wiring or terminal connection (medium)

reading.symptom: After a few minutes of running, it trips the switch and half the house loses power

plan: They asked: "What could cause this?" - answer that first.

Safety: a supply trip hazard is active. The fixed safety warning is shown separately, do not repeat it. It must not be used again until a qualified engineer has checked it: say that plainly. You may explain the likely cause and suggest checks that are safe with it switched off and unplugged, but never say or imply that a check could make it safe to use, or that they might not need an engineer.
Checks they have done and what they found: Reset the trip switch 3 times tonight - It trips again after the oven runs for a few minutes.
Already given by the customer, never ask for it again: make Hotpoint.
The fault they reported is: "After a few minutes of running, it trips the switch and half the house loses power". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.
They asked about something unsafe (repeated reset): do not explain how to do it; the fixed safety wording is shown separately. Offer the safe alternative.

Stage 2: the checks they reported did not fix it. Give the next check that best separates the remaining likely causes, or say what the likely faulty part is if the checks already point to one. Until a check has confirmed which part has failed, name it as the likely part and the check that would confirm it; do not tell them to buy, order or replace it.
